Some of these tips will also apply to the Trezor Chrome extension which can be used offline and works like myTREZOR but without the wallet features. For details about which apps support the Trezor check out the support document - http://doc.satoshilabs.com/trezor-apps/index.html
Would you recommend using the Trezor for long-term cold storage? Or would creating a paper wallet, with an offline computer, with BIP-38 encrypted private key be a better solution?

If you already have experience with that kind of set up and you're fine using an air gap etc then I see no reason to stop using that method if you're happy with it. I would recommend the Trezor as being for newbies (Less skilled with security) or for advanced users who just want convenience.

I view the Trezor as being like a paper wallet you can safely spend from using any online computer without the risk of the private keys being exposed.

This makes it a good option for saving and spending from the same wallet. To separate things you could use the passphrase feature and have different wallets using only 1 Trezor. This is however an advanced feature and I would recommend testing it out first with small amounts. Basically the passphrase acts as a 25th word to the 24 words the Trezor will generate as a recovery seed and the Trezor doesn't store any passphrase's you use.

For the truly paranoid you can set up a Trezor offline and then treat it in the same way as a paper wallet. Then when you come to move/spend bitcoin you don't have to mess about with the air gap/importing keys etc, so it adds convenience. This can be done using command line tools or using the recently released Chrome extension.

I think its worth pointing out that the micro USB cable included in the box is piss poor, this caused a lot of people to have problems with wallets not loading etc. Trezor now comes with a better cable or you could use your own as long as the micro USB cable you have provides data and power.

The other complaints I've seen have been with the myTrezor.com web wallet but I think things have improved now and you of course don't have to use it. As mentioned above you could use the Chrome extension to set up the Trezor and then use it with another app like Electrum.

Using the Trezor with Electrum can be a little confusing on the initial set up, with a Trezor already set up and connected you would open Electrum and chose the "Create new wallet" option and select "Hardware wallet". Basically if Electrum asks you to enter the seed you have selected the wrong option, you should never type the Trezor seed into a computer only if you need to restore a wallet and then using the correct software the seed will be typed in a jumbled order.
